items.issues: Opening 'as if doing violence to himself' reads as forced resolve; distractors each invert a detail (joyful reunion, calm voyage, trust). Slightly abstract wording for easy.
Clear paragraph-level shift from meditation to action; C reverses direction, B misreads the women/men aside.
Final sentence broadens to manners; distractors contradict the passage's stance. Passage contains dated 'race temperament' remark.
Straightforward; distractors invent details (hostile people, lost horses, fertile country).
Clean two-part structure; D is a partial-detail distractor but the refusal is absent.
Correct option is slightly longer/more neutral in phrasing but not giveaway; distractors all contradict events.
B is a sequence reversal, C/D fabricate; fine for easy.
Function is explicit ('I think it would be safest'); D directly contradicted by 'going it blind'.
Sentence is the cause anchoring the resolve; distractors clearly off (forest, search, forgiveness).
Dense philosophical passage raises reading load above easy, though the function itself is clear; C tempts via 'conclusion' in final paragraph.
Correct option is the only compound/nuanced one and longest; A, B, D are flat wrong-emotion distractors, easily eliminated.
'Painful', 'pitiful and grief-stricken' make D direct; subject is likely a dog, which does not affect the answer.
Three distractors are all negative/neutral attitudes with no textual hook; only one positive option exists so it is answerable without reading closely.
C is a modest trap from the quoted line about meanness; others contradict. Very easy.
Two-part attitude stated explicitly; D plays off 'doubt' wording. Narrator gender ('She') assumed by options, not stated in passage.
C is a decent tone-inversion trap; A/B contradict the text.
Correct option is the only one with a qualifying 'though' clause and is longest; A is an overstatement trap, C/D contradict.
'Breathless' appears verbatim in the passage and in the key; distractors are all opposite-valence with no support.
Nearly literal phrase; B is a mild misread of 'brave'. Fine for easy.
Key is the only option containing 'loyally' (allegiance synonym) and is the longest; A/D borrow hospital/line details superficially.
